source.title: Accelerating Greedy Coordinate Gradient and General Prompt Optimization via Probe Sampling
source.authors: Yi-Ran Zhao; Wenyue Zheng; Tianle Cai; Do Xuan Long; Kenji Kawaguchi; Anirudh Goyal; M. Shieh

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates adversarial prompt attacks against aligned models and reports harmful-output attack success rates, testing whether such attacks can bypass refusal. Its main contribution is accelerating the search, not reproducing the original fine-tuning or token-position experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASR for GCG and related jailbreak attacks, which bears on V4. It does not measure KL by response position, prefill compliant openings, change decoding, fine-tune models, or analyze safety-related weights or training objectives. Speed, FLOPs, memory, prompt-learning accuracy, and cited findings are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper speeds up GCG suffix search (probe sampling). Its question is speed. ASR serves as a check that the faster method still works. Plain GCG ASR on Llama2-7b-Chat and Vicuna is a baseline reproduced from Zou et al. The study runs no test of whether suffixes, prefills or decoding defeat refusal by getting past the opening tokens. Most rows are ablations of its own method. Harmfulness is judged only by refusal-string matching.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Probe sampling accelerates GCG 2.1-6.3× on AdvBench with equal or better ASR, and also accelerates AutoPrompt, APE and AutoDAN. The authors make no claim about how deep safety alignment runs.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes adversarial suffixes and accelerates that search; it does not use fine-tuning, token-position KL analysis, compliant-opening prefills, or safety deepening.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success and speed vary with filtered-set reduction R, fixed versus adaptive agreement scoring, probe-set size, and draft-model choice.
record.problems: ASR is defined using rejection phrases, which the authors acknowledge is not a perfect measure. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the ASR results. Some table layouts are compact; the extracted ASR values above are limited to values assigned by the text or table headings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional ASR rows were omitted. Results for AutoDAN and prompt-learning tasks were not included because they are not reported as GCG suffix ASR results bearing directly on V4; other metrics such as time, FLOPs, memory, and accuracy do not measure the claimed safety behaviour.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models by response position.
Whether suffixes work by getting past the opening tokens. Prefilling and decoding changes are not studied. GCG ASR appears only as a baseline for speed comparisons, judged by refusal-string matching.

missing.what: Plain GCG ASR on Vicuna-7b-v1.3 (Strings 88.0; Behaviors 99.0 individual, 98.0 multiple test) and GCG + Annealing baselines
Transfer ASR of GCG suffixes from Llama2-7b-Chat to Vicuna-7b (89.0) and Mistral-7b (86.0)

record.verdict_notes: The study is a speed method for GCG, so it is classed as T4 and gets no verdicts. Several of the record's row values are wrong. r2 and r4 use PS + Annealing numbers that the prose cites as probe sampling. r8 should be 85.0, not 89.0. r7 duplicates r5. ASR uses refusal-substring matching, which the authors call imperfect, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Compliant-opening prefills and decoding changes; the study tests optimized adversarial prompts, not whether getting past the first response tokens is the causal mechanism.
Localization of safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause shallow safety behaviour.
Training to deepen safety across response tokens and whether it holds up.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GCG-optimized adversarial suffixes on Llama2-7b-Chat, including the reported Human Strings and Human Behaviors settings
reader_labels.reason: The study reports substantial harmful-output ASRs for GCG and probe-sampling attacks, including 57.0 and 84.0 for GCG and 64.0 and 91.0 with probe sampling; see r1-r4.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Probe-sampling validation ablations and draft-model choices
reader_labels.reason: Attack success varies by setting: some ASRs are lower than the GCG reference, including R=64, Pearson agreement, B/64, and the Flan-T5 draft; see r11, r23, r26, and r34.
